newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ long bonds rally to end at 3-1/2 year lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ long bonds rally to end at 3-1/2 year lows.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.84 (PREV 92.71) 90-DAYS 7.70 (PREV 7.76)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.05 PCT (PREV 7.70) US 5-YR 6.09 (PREV 6.15)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 765.43 (PREV 766.87) Reuters NZ MCI -59 vs -58
New Zealand long bond yields rallied nearly 20 basis points on Thursday to hit levels not seen since February 1994.
The market was paid early with the tone set by a strong U.S. treasuries market and shorts were scrambling to cover through the session.
"The locals had gone into the CPI long, squared up after the market backed up, got caught short and the covering was pretty frantic," said a Wellington bank chief dealer.
"Locals don't own the market so there isn't any selling from local domestics. There isn't any supply in the domestic market."
The benchmark 11/06 long bond closed at 6.62 percent from Wednesday's 6.80 level.
Even the short end rallied with the September bills futures 13 points stronger at 92.84 as traders took confidence from the partial recovery of the New Zealand dollar.
The market took encouragement from weak retail sales and unemployment data that backed its views that the economy was weaker than the Reserve Bank thinks.
"It pretty much confirmed what the market had thought. It was very supportive of the bullish fever," said a bond dealer.

However, RBNZ Economics Manager Adrian Orr said the bank had not been derailed from its view on the economy, saying that the latest data did not contradict it but it remained on what he called "creditwatch" regarding economic data.
The market has mixed views on whether the bank will alter its view of monetary conditions.
Some doubt it will change from its view that the Monetary Conditions Index should average 825 through the September quarter, while others believe the bank must change.

"The bank is not a million miles away from acting in terms of an MCI easing. We think the data suggests they have enough evidence to do something. Both the QSBO and the retail sales were appalling pieces of data," said the chief dealer.
Some banks also commented that mortgage rates would be under upward pressure soon if there was no downward correction to bill market rates.
